headline: Google's Gemini-based math agents have reportedly proved several math problems that were still unsolved, with automatic checking software confirming the proofs.
score_reason: Headline says five problems but the article's own figures differ, the work dates from mid-2026 or earlier, and only one crypto-news outlet reports it.
importance_line: Mathematicians and researchers in other fields could gain a cheap way to find and check proofs (the article says a few hundred dollars per problem), but the numbers are unclear, the work is not new today, and people still have to judge whether a result is truly new.
summary: Crypto Briefing reports that Google DeepMind's Gemini-based AI agents, whose answers are graded by automatic proof checkers, have found proofs for puzzles that were still open, including 9 of the 353 problems on a well-known list of unsolved math questions (two of the nine had stood for 56 years). The article's own figures (9, 44 and 13) do not match its headline of five, they come from work dated mid-2026 or earlier, and it says people must still confirm that a result is really new.
freshness: FOLLOW-UP of mid-2026 (exact date not stated)
notes: Secondary source; DeepMind's own paper was not read. Work is older than 2 Oct 2026 and no exact date is given. Score lowered 8 to 6.
